Hola a tod@s!

@Pepa Montero Jimena, @Enrique Diaz Blanco, @Juanjo Madrigal, @Jorge Luis Mayoral Perez and myself are meeting this Wednesday at the faculty of mathematics of Universidad Complutense at 18:00 to organize Madrid Lean meetings (MadLean). If anyone is interested in helping us organize, please DM me or any of the above people to coordinate. Thanks!

PS: would it be possible to rename this topic to Madrid, Spain or Madrid, ES for clarity?
Exact location and time confirmed! We have reserved aula 113 of the faculty of mathematics from 18:00-20:00.

My co-organizers and I are delighted to announce MadLean, the first Lean Meetup in Madrid!

It will take place this Wednesday at 18:00-19:30 at the Faculty of Mathematics of the Universidad Complutense (room TBA but probably 113).

The rough plan is to:

  • Assist with Lean installation :computer:.
  • Show newcomers how to do simple proofs :check:.
  • Share our Lean tooling :tools:.
  • Discuss projects we are working on :light_bulb:.
  • Hang out and have a good atmosphere while learning together :blush:.

Everyone is welcome to attend!

Poster by our very own @Pepa Montero Jimena
Aw man, I wish I was in Madrid more often and I could join. I notice nobody in this Spain topic is sending others a :octopus: emoji. :wink: :rolling_on_the_floor_laughing:

Poster by @Pepa Montero Jimena.

https://madlean-hub.web.app/

Very cool!
Question: is the thesis unrelated to Mathlib? Because Mathlib had Urysohn's lemma since 2021 (docs#exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed / mathlib3#6967). Though only one side of it IIUC?

Hi @Snir Broshi! The thesis is not unrelated to Mathlib, I used Mathlib objects for my formalization and proof, but I was prompted by my supervisor to try to write it myself without looking at Mathlib's.

From the docs you mentioned I copied this extract: "Most paper sources prove Urysohn's lemma using a family of open sets indexed by dyadic rational numbers on [0, 1]. There are many technical difficulties with formalizing this proof (e.g., one needs to formalize the "dyadic induction", then prove that the resulting family of open sets is monotone). So, we formalize a slightly different proof."

Essentially, I did not realize there was an easier way of formalizing it, so I followed the traditional proof mentioned here and ran into the problems they describe (and overcame them!). So my proof is different from the one in Mathlib.
Nice job!
Thank you! :))

Just letting people know the room will be announced last minute this week.

There’s been an administrative hiccup, but @Pepa Montero Jimena and I are meeting with the vice-dean of the university this week at the beginning of the meetup in order to ask for more resources, so hopefully this shouldn’t happen again!

Meetup will start on time with @Enrique Diaz Blanco @Juanjo Madrigal present :gift_heart:.

Title:
Verso Blueprints: Reimagining Blueprints for The AI Era

Abstract:
Blueprints have become an important tool for guiding mathematical formalization: they provide a shared plan, organize the relationship between informal exposition and formal developments, and help coordinate collaboration between mathematicians and formalizers. The LeanBlueprint project was a major success in this direction, establishing blueprints as a practical and widely adopted interface for planning, tracking, and communicating Lean formalization projects. A recent key success story is the sphere packing blueprint, whose structured exposition helped guide the autoformalization of the proof and demonstrated the value of blueprints as a bridge between mathematics, formalization, and automation.

In this talk, we present Verso Blueprints, a new blueprint toolchain built in and for Lean. Verso is a Lean-based system for writing extensible, elaborated documents, where mathematical text and document structure can interact directly with Lean. Verso Blueprints combine blueprint-style project organization with Verso’s document model and Lean’s elaboration mechanisms, enabling rich mathematical structure, extensible documents, and automatically synchronized metadata connected to the formalization.

We will explain what Verso Blueprints are, describe their main novelties, and outline the roadmap ahead. In particular, we will discuss how Verso Blueprints aim to support smooth collaboration between mathematicians, formalizers, and emerging LLM-based tools for formalization and de-formalization.

Event has been crossposted on #Event announcements > MadLean Seminars.

Next session @Julian Berman will present his hobbyist kernel project rpylean. We are planning for an accessible, interactive talk that is beginner-friendly. :smile:

Lean is made up of a small trusted kernel responsible for type checking what you write, or equivalently verifying what you prove. The Lean developers encourage other people to write their own independently-trusted kernels. We'll talk about a hobbyists' kernel called rpylean which was written to learn more about Lean's internals and the type checking process overall.

Hi everyone! I'm Miguel. My background is in computer science and formal methods. Looking forward to engaging more with mathematics through Lean. Really like the MadLean initiative! :blush:

Hey! I just found out about this tool https://github.com/argumentcomputer/ix that you may find interesting. It basically allows you to compress any Lean4 proof into a short "digest" that you can verify in a "short" amount of time (where the exact meaning of "short" can vary depending on the backend you choose, but it may even reach constant time with respect to the size of the original proof!!). So you could for example compress the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem and write it by hand in any margin you want ;)
